subject: DELETE statement
notes: Read FileRegistry.DeleteFile: 'if (!File.Exists(c.HostPath)) status = FileStatusCode.OptionalFileNotFound;' with OptionalFileNotFound = \"05\" (FileStatus.cs), reached only after the '41' and '62' guards, and assigned as the ordinary (non-throwing) outcome so it is treated as SUCCESS downstream. The success classification is load-bearing and is implemented: KeyedIoEmitter.EmitDeleteFile branches on 'st[0] != \'0\'' for ON EXCEPTION, so '05' takes the NOT ON EXCEPTION arm, and its comment states the rule ('\'05\' (absent file) is a SUCCESSFUL completion (GR14) and takes the NOT ON EXCEPTION path'). Two spec-derived goldens close it: tests/conformance/2023/delete_file_absent.cob deletes a never-created file with both phrases written and its .out is exactly 'NOEXC' + 'ST=05' -- proving both the value and the success classification; tests/conformance/2023/delete_file_sharing.cob re-deletes an already-deleted file and pins 'DEL05=05'. DESIGN-SPEC-RECONCILIATION row 20 records the earlier wrong claim (that a missing file gave '35') as repaired, and docs/FILES_DESIGN.md:117 now states the rule correctly. || UPHELD: the success CLASSIFICATION, which is the half that can silently go wrong, I validated independently against the spec rather than against the code comment -- cite.py --check 9.1.13.2 -> 'OK 9.1.13.2 4) b) For a DELETE FILE statement, the referenced file is not available', and 9.1.13.2 is titled 'Successful completion', so '05' is a success-class status and the NOT ON EXCEPTION routing is right. Both goldens are registered and actually run (tests/conformance/2023/manifest.json:35-36; ConformanceTests.cs:241,244) and I read their .out files: 'NOEXC' + 'ST=05', and 'DEL05=05'.
